Priya —

Quick sync from our side before next week's kickoff: thanks again for sharing the Orion launch timeline. To avoid any last‑minute throttling during the phased rollout, we need your best guess on concurrent API TPS, expected peak daily tokens, and any important cadence (e.g., large night batches). I attached the template (orion_traffic_forecast_v1.xlsx) — if you can fill the cells for Week 0 (pilot) and Week 1–4 (ramp) that'd be ideal.

On our side: we plan to request a temporary quota exception for a 2x burst for the first 48 hours of the public launch, then a 1.4x sustained bump for the following two weeks. That request will include fallback routing to a cheaper quantized model for non-critical paths.

Next steps I propose:
- Priya: provide forecast by EOD Thursday (we can accept ranges)
- Marissa: confirm whether product can tolerate the cheaper fallback for non-auth calls
- Karthik/Dev: estimate infra lead time for quota change and any other entitlements we need to set up (billing/project limits)

Thanks — we'll use this thread as the operational record.

Hi Sergio —

Thanks — attaching what I have so far (high level numbers):
- Pilot (internal beta, 48h): peak concurrent TPS ~32, estimated peak tokens/hour ~1.1M
- Week 1 (public rollout): expected peak concurrent TPS ~90, peak tokens/hour ~3.5M, sustained 16–20 TPS
- Week 2–4 (growth): burst windows up to 180 TPS for short periods (3–6 hours) during promo events; otherwise sustained ~40 TPS

Notes: these are conservative to the best of our telemetry. We do have a nightly batch that submits ~250k records between 02:00–03:00 ET (small latency tolerance).

We filed a request with our infra team to surface any third‑party rate limits that could affect retries; will share updates if anything changes.

Thanks Priya and Sergio — good context. A couple of product questions before we greenlight the fallback:

1) Which call paths can degrade to the quantized model without regulatory/logging differences? Specifically, will clinical decisioning calls need full FP32 for auditability?
2) Can you flag which endpoints are high‑priority (low latency) vs background (batchable)? We'll map those to routing policies.

From a rollout perspective: we prefer the 48h 2x burst to be limited to authenticated production keys only (no staging). Also, if you expect promo windows, please mark them in the spreadsheet — promo bursts are when we need headroom.

I can approve the exception from product if the degraded model is only used for non‑clinical inference and if logs/metadata remain identical.

Quick infra check — numbers look reasonable but a few operational constraints: 

- Lead time: we can provision the temporary quota exception in ~36–48 hours once finance/billing signoff is recorded against the Acme tenant. If Acme requests a new reserved project or billing commit, that adds 3–5 business days.
- Burst headroom: a 2x burst for 48h is achievable if we pin them to a dedicated pool slice and set autoscale thresholds accordingly. That requires a short maintenance window to update routing policies (~30 minutes off-peak).
- Nightly batch: we'll set a low-priority class with batching enabled for the 02:00–03:00 ET job to reduce tokens/cost. That requires client-side header to mark the calls as background.

Action items for us:
- Dev: prepare quota change playbook + scripts (Proj: ORION-D-4729)
- Karthik: coordinate billing flag with Finance and schedule maintenance window

If you want, I can draft the exception PDF for legal/finance to sign.
